body_text:
The *determinant* $\det : M_{n \times n}(F) \to F$ is the unique
multilinear, alternating function of the column vectors that assigns
the value $1$ to the identity matrix $I_n$.

It is given explicitly by the Leibniz formula:
$$ \det(A) = \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) \prod_{i=1}^n A_{\sigma(i), i}. $$

The determinant possesses fundamental algebraic properties:
1. Multiplicativity: $\det(AB) = \det(A) \det(B)$.
2. Invertibility: A square matrix $A$ is invertible in $M_{n \times n}(F)$
   if and only if $\det(A) \neq 0$.
3. Geometric volume: Over $\mathbb{R}$, $|\det(A)|$ measures the volume
   scaling factor of the parallelotope spanned by the column vectors.
4. Similarity invariance: $\det(P^{-1}AP) = \det(A)$, proving that the
   determinant is an intrinsic invariant of a linear operator $T$,
   independent of the choice of basis.
